subject.title: [Bug] TTS audio content cross-talk between concurrent sessions in the same process (private audio delivered to wrong recipient)

question: Should the Microsoft TTS fallback receive immediate provider-specific concurrency containment while maintainers reproduce the alleged cross-recipient disclosure?
rationale: The report alleges private data disclosure on the latest stable release, but current evidence does not identify whether the defect is in node-edge-tts, OpenClaw synthesis orchestration, or outbound delivery; choosing temporary containment versus observation changes both security exposure and user latency.

options.title: Contain Microsoft concurrency
options.body: Temporarily serialize Microsoft provider synthesis only, add explicit diagnostic correlation, and remove the lock if concurrent reproduction proves the provider safe.

options.title: Disable Microsoft fallback
options.body: Remove or disable Microsoft fallback until its concurrent behavior is proven, accepting a more disruptive compatibility change for stronger containment.

options.title: Reproduce before mitigation
options.body: Keep current concurrency while collecting controlled traces, accepting continued exposure if the reported incident is genuine.

recommendation.title: Contain Microsoft concurrency
recommendation.body: Temporarily serialize Microsoft provider synthesis only, add explicit diagnostic correlation, and remove the lock if concurrent reproduction proves the provider safe.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail connects this person to the original Edge fallback behavior and the security-impact choice spans provider policy and stable-release containment.
